(1) Image embed scope gate: src/renderer/src/util/exportImages.js gains a pure scope classifier isInDocumentScope(resolvedPath, baseDir) — separators normalized to '/', trailing-slash-tolerant, segment-boundary prefix match (baseDir '/docs' never claims '/docsfiles/x.png'), case-insensitive only under isWindows() — and embedLocalImages(html, baseDir, { requestScopeConsent } = {}) becomes a two-phase pass: classify first, and when deduplicated out-of-scope candidates (resolvable local paths with a known MIME that WOULD be read) exist, ask the caller once via await requestScopeConsent(candidatePaths); the granted subset (exactly the listed files) embeds through the unchanged stat/cap/read path, everything else out-of-scope keeps its src and counts skipped; with no callback the consent default is declined, so in-scope embedding (corner C-1) and all skip semantics are unchanged while the C-2 absolute-path embed dies. (2) PlantUML export consent, gate location pinned: RENDER-TIME, inside src/muya/lib/utils/exportHtml.js (in ObservedWriteScope), NOT a renderer post-render strip — the deflate+base64url URL cannot be inverted back to source in editor.vue without a net-new inflate dependency, which this boundary change forbids, and muya/lib/index.js stays untouched because Muya#exportStyledHTML(options) already forwards the options bag verbatim into ExportHtml.generate(options), so editor.vue adds one opaque key plantumlRemoteConsent to the calls it already makes in both the styledHtml (editor.vue:2273) and docx (editor.vue:2315) branches; exportHtml.js exports two pure helpers — countPlantUMLFences(markdown) (fenced blocks whose trimmed info string is exactly 'plantuml', ``` and ~~~ fences, fence-state tracked, used by editor.vue to decide whether to ask) and plantUMLSourcePlaceholder(rawCode) (the pinned declined shape: exactly one pre.ag-plantuml-export-source holding the escapeHTML'd literal diagram source, no plantuml.com URL) — and renderDiagram's plantuml branch (exportHtml.js:186-190) calls diagram.insertImgElement(diagramContainer) only when generate() saw plantumlRemoteConsent:true, otherwise it inserts the placeholder; src/muya/lib/parser/render/plantuml.js itself is NOT in the write scope and is not touched (PLANTUML_URL and the remote transport stay as-is; only the export-time disclosure is new), and the live-preview fetch at muya/lib/parser/render/index.js:396 is OUT of scope (editor-preview behavior, own follow-up). T-001.Title: M-065 embed scope gate: pure scope classifier, two-phase consent pass, declined accounting, and the unit matrix re-pinned to consent semantics

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: exportImages.js gains the pure scope classifier beside resolveImageSrc, inside a paired START_BLOCK_SCOPE_GATE / END_BLOCK_SCOPE_GATE block: isInDocumentScope(resolvedPath, baseDir) returns false for a falsy baseDir, normalizes both sides to forward slashes, strips trailing slashes, and requires a segment-boundary prefix match (resolved equals the base or starts with base + '/'; '/docs' never claims '/docsfiles/x.png'), comparing case-insensitively only when isWindows() is true; the classifier reads no DOM, performs no I/O, and resolveImageSrc is untouched (the preserved behaviors stay pinned: remote http(s) and data: sources return null and are untouched, generic UNC passes through uncounted, an untitled document's relative srcs stay uncounted).

embedLocalImages becomes the two-phase consent pass with the exact signature embedLocalImages(html, baseDir, { requestScopeConsent } = {}): phase 1 DOM-walks the imgs and classifies every resolvable local src with a known MIME (IMAGE_MIME_BY_EXT unchanged) — in-scope candidates and all unchanged behaviors proceed exactly as today; out-of-scope candidates are collected deduplicated by resolved path and, when non-empty, logged count-only as [export][embed-images][BLOCK_EMBED_SCOPE_CONSENT outOfScope=N] and then granted = await requestScopeConsent(candidatePaths) — the callback receives the deduplicated resolved-path list and returns the granted subset; with no callback provided the grant is empty (declined-by-default, logged [export][embed-images][BLOCK_EMBED_SCOPE_DECLINED declined=K]). Phase 2 keeps the existing per-path outcome cache and stat → regular-file → EMBED_CAP_BYTES (8 MiB, unchanged) → readBinary → data: URL path for in-scope references and for granted out-of-scope references alike; an out-of-scope reference whose resolved path is not in the grant keeps its src untouched and counts skipped, so embedded/total/skipped accounting stays honest and the caller's existing skipped-notice logic needs no change; no read (stat or readBinary) of any out-of-scope path happens before the consent callback resolves, and declined refs trigger zero I/O; the pass never throws on an image (unchanged).

tests/renderer/util/exportImages.test.js is re-pinned to the consent semantics with the old vulnerable pin REMOVED: the C-2 test body ('embeds an absolute POSIX path and leaves no absolute path in the output (C-2)' against '/irrelevant/base' expecting embedded=1) is deleted and replaced by a consent-semantics pin titled with 're-pinned to consent semantics (C-2)' asserting that the same absolute path against '/irrelevant/base' with no consent callback keeps its src, counts embedded=0 / skipped=1, and triggers no stat — this pin fails on pre-fix code (pre-fix embeds it) and passes post-fix. New describes inside a paired unique test block pin the gate red-first: 'not embed an out-of-scope absolute path without consent' (out-of-scope refused, src survives, skipped counted, no I/O), 'still embeds an in-scope sibling image (C-1 unchanged)' (the corner C-1 relative pin passes byte-for-byte as today), 'embeds exactly the granted subset of the consented list' (a requestScopeConsent granting one of two out-of-scope candidates embeds only the granted one — the second img keeps its src and counts skipped), consent-list integrity (the candidate list the callback receives is deduplicated by resolved path across two spellings plus a file:// form of the same file, one entry), 'grants embed through the unchanged cap and MIME gates' (a granted path at EMBED_CAP_BYTES still skips with SKIP_TOO_BIG semantics and an unknown extension still never embeds), and declined-accounting honesty (declined refs never appear in embedded; total counts them). Every existing corner keeps its assertions unchanged except the explicitly listed pin updates: corner C-2's body is re-pinned as above; the three RESOLUTION pins that observe a normalized absolute path through the embed ('strips file:/// URLs and embeds the referenced file', and the two Windows normalization tests — drive-letter and \?\ extended-prefix, corner C-3 family) keep every assertion byte-identical and change ONLY their call shape, passing a requestScopeConsent that grants the single candidate, because their absolute targets are out-of-scope against the null base by design and the pins exist to pin resolution, not consent; the generic-UNC pin, the dedup corner C-10 (its file:///docs/img/same.png spelling resolves INSIDE '/docs' and stays in-scope), the C-4 decode pin, all skip corners and the markup-integrity pin are untouched. The ipcFs/isWindows mocks are reused as-is.

Gate ordering CAUTION made true in code: the consent callback is awaited strictly between classification and the first out-of-scope I/O, so the dialog the user sees lists exactly the files the pass is about to read; no scope widening (workspace-resident assets are NOT in scope this change — an open workspace does not widen the embed scope), no new dependency, and exportImages.js gains no new import.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The disclosed semantic choice is implemented exactly as pinned: FENCE-AT-M031 (not fs_read_inner) — justification recorded here for the bundle: riding fs_read_inner as-is would (a) route the sidecar through m047_bookmarks::ensure_access bookmark semantics this surface does not declare, (b) replace the strict UTF-8 sidecar failure (V-M-031 F7) with M-014 detect-and-decode bytes-replacement, silently changing diff baseline bytes for legacy-encoded sidecars, and (c) move the error shape off Result<String, String> onto IpcError, changing the renderer's existing baseline-failure catch; fencing at the m031 boundary reuses m010_security::check_path UNCHANGED and keeps read_to_string, preserving F7 byte-for-byte. m031_diff.rs gains a file-header START_MODULE_CONTRACT / START_MODULE_MAP / START_CHANGE_SUMMARY block (none exists today) stating the fenced sidecar read, the denial vocabulary and the untouched git fallback, with exactly ONE CHANGE_SUMMARY line (2026-11-21 C-EXPORT-BOUNDARIES); the #[tauri::command] becomes pub fn mt_diff_baseline(path: String, sec: State<'_, SecurityCtx>) -> Result<String, String> delegating to pub(crate) fn mt_diff_baseline_inner(path: &str, sandbox: &Path) — Tauri injects the State, so diffView.vue's invoke('mt_diff_baseline', { path: pathname }) is unchanged and main.rs (registration at main.rs:982, SecurityCtx already managed) is not touched; no new IPC command.

The fence, in order, on the '{path}.before' sidecar read only: the existing document-path existence check and the BLOCK_DIFF_BASELINE marker stay first and unchanged; when the sidecar exists — (1) m010_security::check_path(sandbox, Path::new(&before_str)) reusing the funnel as-is (lexical, canonical, NUL/overlong, E6 symlink resolved-target semantics included); on SecurityError the command logs [m031][diff][BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=sandbox_violation] and returns Err whose string carries MT_FS_PATH_DENIED and the security error text — no bytes are returned and the git fallback does NOT run on a denial; (2) fs::metadata regular-file gate — a non-regular sidecar (dir, FIFO, symlink-to-dir) logs [m031][diff][BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=not_regular_file] and returns Err carrying MT_FS_NOT_REGULAR; (3) meta.len() > crate::m013b::fs::MAX_READ_BYTES (the reused 10 MiB constant) logs [m031][diff][BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=oversize] and returns Err carrying MT_FS_TOO_LARGE with the byte figures; (4) std::fs::read_to_string(&validated) — the strict UTF-8 read on the validated path, keeping today's Err('Failed to read .before file: …') on invalid UTF-8 (F7 preserved, no decode-and-replace); a valid in-sandbox sidecar reads exactly as before (BLOCK_DIFF_BASELINE_OK source=before bytes=… unchanged). The git-show fallback (_diff_git_baseline) and the app-store refusal branch are byte-identical to today, and the raw unfenced form std::fs::read_to_string(before_path) no longer exists in the file.

The in-file test module moves onto sandbox-rooted fixtures and gains the red-first fence pins: every std::env::temp_dir() usage is replaced by a TempDir sandbox root (tempfile, already a dev-dependency of the funnel suites' convention) with the document and its .before sidecar written inside it, calling mt_diff_baseline_inner directly (no Tauri State needed) — baseline_nonexistent_file_returns_err, baseline_assembles_git_show_command (#[cfg(not(feature = "app-store"))], assertion shape unchanged) and baseline_before_file_takes_priority keep their behavioral assertions on the new roots; baseline_current_repo_file is unchanged. New pins: baseline_sidecar_outside_sandbox_denied (a {path}.before symlink resolving OUTSIDE the TempDir sandbox yields Err containing MT_FS_PATH_DENIED — fails pre-fix because pre-fix returns the file's bytes — and the error is not Ok content), baseline_sidecar_symlink_inward_reads (a symlink resolving INSIDE the sandbox reads normally — deny-only-NEW-links spirit: pre-existing inward resolution is allowed), baseline_sidecar_non_regular_denied (a directory named {path}.before → Err with MT_FS_NOT_REGULAR), baseline_sidecar_over_cap_denied (a sidecar sized past the cap via file.set_len(MAX_READ_BYTES + 1) — no 10 MiB write — → Err with MT_FS_TOO_LARGE), and baseline_invalid_utf8_sidecar_still_errors (invalid UTF-8 bytes in the sidecar → Err('Failed to read .before file: …'), the honest F7 pin that fences the funnel-reuse alternative out).
